question: A colleague reports that Claude gave them an incorrect answer inside a shared project. What should the project owner do first?
options: A) Remove every document from the knowledge base and rebuild the project from current files.
B) Rewrite the project instructions to add a rule that all answers must be double-checked by hand.
C) Advise the colleague to try the same question again in a new chat within the same project.
D) Ask which question was asked, then check the uploaded documents for the answer Claude gave.
correct_answers: D) Ask which question was asked, then check the uploaded documents for the answer Claude gave.
explanations: Rebuilding everything is disproportionate before the cause is even known.
A blanket caution does not diagnose or fix whatever produced the wrong answer.
The same project knowledge is read again, so a retry rarely changes a source-driven error.
Correct. Tracing the answer back to a source separates a stale document from a prompting or model problem.
